items.question: Can a shipped option or method drop a cached flag and later callback value without changing session or distinct identity?
items.answer: Cache drop without identity rotation established: true. Successful exact calls: updateFlags({}, {}, {merge:false}); featureFlags.updateFlags({}, {}, {merge:false}); featureFlags.receivedFeatureFlags({featureFlags:{}, featureFlagPayloads:{}, flags:{}}).
items.method: Each trial first fetches warm-response from the local flags route. Both disables are then true before the candidate is called. Read-back, a newly registered real onFeatureFlags callback, session ID and distinct ID are observed. featureFlags.reset is the positive control for a retained cache.

findings.observation: No person-free enabled evaluation was established in the concrete init/set_config matrix; prohibited containers or address data remain, or no enabled request was observed.
featureFlags.reset() invalidates pending evaluations but retains a populated flag cache.
unregister("$enabled_feature_flags") hides ordinary values but leaves warm-response in detailed getters; it is not a qualifying cache drop.
A cache-drop call alone admits a held old reply; featureFlags.reset() followed by the call rejects that reply and permits a fresh reply, without rotating identity.

Flags-only adapter withdrawal leaves the synthetic consent key at 0, while original E5 enables autocapture/replay and removes it. Different fixture configurations prevent attributing that difference to the candidate; before/after candidate storage stays unchanged.
Memory persistence still leaves the synthetic opt-in consent key in localStorage. The successful cache-drop calls do not change that finding.

runHistory.observed: E18–E20 missing after item-list extension; expected guard failure.
Symlinked dependency resolution failed the normal-module-entry assertion before browser tests.
After using independent pinned dependencies, the anchored full-title filter found no tests.
17 tests passed; E1 exceeded the original 45-second budget. Those 17 answers matched the original record.

E1 passed with its unchanged assertions and 120-second budget; its answer matched. E19 passed. E18 exceeded its first 240-second matrix budget, so dependent E20 had no E18 result. No SDK result inferred from those failures.
99-case preliminary request matrix and side-effect test passed with flags-only contexts and a 600-second matrix budget.
Detailed getters reject partial cache removal; all three remaining candidates passed storage, full-reset/idle, lazy-load, disabled-request and warmed delayed-reply probes.
An incorrect expected null at flags-only adapter withdrawal was corrected to the observed 0. Measurement data was not changed; the original E5 fixture configuration difference is explicit.

Flags-only extension fixtures omit recorder pre-import while retaining the normal SDK module. Original fixtures and measurement assertions are retained; session budgets and failed runs are recorded.
The integration option uses a local synthetic analytics-user object accepted by its shipped declaration; no external integration SDK or service is involved.
Response-ingestion and direct SDK method calls are diagnostic facts, not an adapter change or an enabled attestation. Product flags remain at control.
Per-method storage records cover the listed lifecycle phases; other markup, tabs, SDK versions and longer time windows are outside this experiment.
